SMTO-GML-0068 — Some emails didn't end up the way SMTO expected

GUID: c29da131-e11e-4e99-b49d-ddea519fb95a
Slug: gmail-selected-state-verification-failed
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-client-actions

What happened

  • SMTO changed your emails, but when it checked afterward, some weren't in the expected state, for example another app or a Gmail filter moved them again. Changes Gmail confirmed are kept; nothing is repeated automatically.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the result SMTO reported for this Task: how many emails were changed, unchanged or failed. Those numbers show how much of the work already happened.
  2. Open Gmail and look at a few of the emails that should have changed: are they archived, labeled or in Trash as you asked? Another app, your phone or a Gmail filter may have changed them again after SMTO did.
  3. Ask SMTO to change only the emails that still aren't right, by naming them or using a narrow search. Repeating the whole request could redo or undo changes that already worked.
  4. If this was a reply and archive, your reply was already sent; ask only for the archiving, not a new reply. Only the archiving step is in question, and sending again would deliver two copies.

What success looks like

  • In Gmail, every email you meant to change is in the expected state, or SMTO clearly lists the ones that remain.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Task's reported counts, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat the whole request until you've checked which emails already changed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Post-write verification of the frozen Gmail message IDs found messages without the intended labels (or still present after deletion) after all batches were acknowledged; acknowledged counts are kept and the operation is marked incomplete.

What this means

  • Verification checks the frozen IDs for intended labels or disappearance. Concurrent changes or provider behavior can cause a mismatch; acknowledged changed counts are retained and completion stays false.

Why this can happen

  • Verification checks the frozen IDs for intended labels or disappearance. Concurrent changes or provider behavior can cause a mismatch; acknowledged changed counts are retained and completion stays false.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected account, action arguments and operation reference; do not infer mailbox effects from the error alone.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the operation result (changed, unchanged, failed and unknown counts) and the current labelIds of the selected IDs; look for concurrent clients, Gmail filters or provider delay. Request only the remaining discrepancies with an explicit narrower selection; never replay the whole compound action or resend a confirmed reply.
  • Inspect the saved operation and current state of its selected messages before deciding which remaining work to request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the saved operation and current state of its selected messages before deciding which remaining work to request.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected IDs have the intended state or the remaining discrepancy is explicitly reported.

What not to do

  • Do not resend a successful reply or treat new arrivals as a failed initial selection.

Technical notes

  • Previously acknowledged changes remain confirmed; missing acknowledgments remain unknown. No automatic replay is authorized.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
